To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have shown efficient coupling via a silica nanowire to photonic crystal nanocavities, and that we have shown that the nanowire micro-loops can be used to couple light from a photonic crystal waveguide to a nanocavity, with a measured coupling efficiency of 0.4%.

We demonstrate efficient coupling via an optical fiber taper to a photonic-crystal-based nanocavity containing a single quantum dot, specifically designed for applications in single photon source devices.
the coupling efficiency from tapered nanowire micro-loops to photonic crystal nanocavities can reach 90% and the quantum dot emission can be enhanced by a factor of 2.2.

the development and characterization of photonic crystal based nanostructures for single photon source application.
the design and fabrication of photonic crystal nanocavities for quantum information processing.
the design and fabrication of nanoscale devices for single-photon source applications.

this thesis demonstrates the first experimental realization of a nanowire micro-ring resonator with the ability to couple to a photonic nanocavity.

we have demonstrated efficient coupling via a micro-loop to a nanocavity containing single photon sources, which is an important milestone towards the realization of a quantum dot coupled single photon source for quantum communication applications.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated efficient coupling of light from a tapered silica nanofibre to a photonic nanocavity containing a single emitter.
we demonstrate efficient coupling to a photonic-crystal nanocavity containing InAs quantum dots, by using a silica nanowire taper.
we have shown how to couple to photonic crystals in a more efficient and robust way than what has been previously reported in the literature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nanowire micro-loops provide a robust and reliable way to couple light into photonic crystal nanocavities with a high efficiency.

a tapered nanowire loop can efficiently couple to a high Q nanocavity, and that the coupling can be tuned via a combination of the taper radius, the nanocavity design, and the nanocavity position relative to the nanowire loop.
a single nanowire microloop can be used to simultaneously excite and collect photons from the nanocavity.
